title: How many overflow blocks an import 3PL beside the San Pedro Bay ports should take for January to June 2027 after customers front-loaded ahead of a duty increase
subdomain: fulfillment-warehousing (an import 3PL's commitment to overflow storage blocks for January to June 2027 after its customers front-loaded imports ahead of a duty increase)
prompt_shape: a count of overflow blocks to take for a half-year term, with the import TEU and port share of January to October 2026 (twenty figures, charted)

sources.origin: constructed for this task by task161/generator/build.py (seeded, deterministic) around a fictional import 3PL (Pellerin Distribution Services) with four buildings in Carson, Rancho Dominguez, Wilmington and Compton, its clients, people and systems, a fictional industrial landlord (Ridley-Ames Industrial Properties) and park (Tamarind Avenue Logistics Park), a fictional customs broker (Yamamoto & Vance Customs Brokers) and transload partner (Avila Transload Services); no real company, person or system is depicted. The two ports' monthly statistics for 2026 are constructed in the layout of each port's public release and are not the ports' published figures. The broker's advisories describe the 2019 and 2025 United States duty changes in general terms; the duty increase of 1 January 2027 is fictional. Container owner prefixes, carriers, vessels and terminal names are used descriptively.
